neighbours.label: ' the' right after a preposition that places an event or activity somewhere (played on the piano, sat by the lake, won on the final day); ' the' after a verb or at the start of a clause stays quiet
fire: After supper my grandfather played a few old hymns on the organ in the chapel.
Last summer the two sisters spent every afternoon reading by the lake near their cabin.
She broke the school record in the long jump on the second day of the championships.
When the music started, the couple danced slowly on the terrace under the lanterns.
Our team lost narrowly to the visitors on the road last Saturday night.
He found his old friend sitting alone by the fountain in the square.
The young pianist performed a nocturne on the grand piano at the festival.
We relaxed for a while by the fire after a long day of skiing.
quiet: After supper my grandfather opened the hymnbook and chose a few old songs.
Last summer the two sisters finally finished reading the whole series.
